note: Whole screens built to Tattva's rules, one per product type. Copy the structure, then check your screen against it.

screens.title: Agent console (an agent that writes emails to customers; a person approves each one)
why: The plan is visible before and during the work: StepTimeline shows what is done, what is waiting and what is next.

Nothing that cannot be undone happens without a yes: ApprovalPrompt states exactly what will be sent, to whom, with equal Approve and Deny. Amber appears only here, because only here a person has to act.
The draft says it was written by the AI (AILabel), and why the agent wrote it.
Every decision lands in ActionLog: who approved it, when, and whether it can be undone. Sent email cannot.
On a phone the plan stacks above the draft; nothing is hidden behind hover.

screens.title: AI dashboard (what a team spends on AI each month)
why: The numbers that matter first are tiles with their change and which direction is good (spend going up is bad).
Every chart sits in ChartFrame: a title, one sentence saying what it shows, the source, and a table view, so the numbers are readable without seeing colour.
A limit is a Meter that turns amber near the limit, with the number in words.
Sample figures are labelled as sample.

screens.title: Chat assistant (a hotel finder)
why: The first screen is never empty: EmptyState says what the assistant can do, with three starters.
Answers that recommend things are cards, not paragraphs: CardRow of ResultCards with the same facts each, so people compare like with like. On a phone the row swipes and the next card peeks in.
Every fact that came from somewhere has a numbered CitationMarker and a SourceList under the answer.
The assistant says it is an AI once, quietly (AIDisclosure in the footnote), not on every message.
Feedback sits under the answer, after the person has read it. Book is the only action on a card.
Sample data is labelled as sample until a real model and hotel data are connected.

screens.title: Creative tool (pictures from text for a bakery's posts)
why: One prompt box with real examples, and settings people understand (shape, look), each with its cost shown before Generate, so nobody is surprised by what a run spends.
Progress is honest: GenerationProgress says what is happening and can be cancelled.
Several variations side by side (VariantGrid), one chosen at a time, marked as AI-made (AILabel).
Nothing is lost: earlier results stay one tap away.

screens.title: Generative UI (the assistant asks what it needs, then answers in parts)
why: When the request is unclear, the assistant asks instead of guessing: QuestionSet, one question at a time, with a recommended option, You decide, Use the defaults and a last look before sending.
The answer arrives in Sections that open as they stream, so a long answer stays readable.
After answering, the questions shrink to a Receipt so the thread stays short.
